judged_text: Guests silently dropped by the filter (already attendees, or blacklisted) are never reported back — the API returns success for the survivors with no indication of which requested guests were skipped. A user who pastes a list where some emails are already attendees sees 'Guests added' and has no way to know part of their input was discarded; if they later re-submit the dropped ones expecting clarity, they hit the misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error instead of an explanation.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the server silently filters out requested guests that are already attendees or blacklisted (`uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)`), but still returns success (`return { message: "Guests added" }`) with no info about skipped emails. Worse, when all requested emails are filtered out (`uniqueGuests.length === 0`), it throws `BAD_REQUEST` with message `"emails_must_be_unique_valid"`, which is misleading because the failure can be due to "already an attendee" or "blacklisted" rather than invalid/non-unique emails. The client always shows a generic success toast (`showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")`) and never reports partial skips.
